## Objective
- Build “Tunis Moto Life,” a lightweight, playable 3D open-world driving prototype for Android and iOS, set in a Tunisian city.
- Deliver offline free ride with vehicles, mobile controls, progression, customization, and saved player data.

## Requirements
- Third-person driving, mobile performance and touch controls, Tunis-inspired streets and buildings, traffic signals, streetlights, and day/night cycle.
- Motorcycles with manual 6-speed transmission, clutch, RPM/speedometer, wheelie, burnout, steering, and braking; cars, dealership, garage, vehicle buying, tuning, and customization.
- Earn in-game money through driving and persist player progress and inventory.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-based Three.js prototype with localStorage saves and procedural low-poly city and vehicle assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game UI in `index.html` and `styles.css`, and implemented procedural city, vehicles, menus, driving, controls, progression, customization, and saves in `game.js`.
- Fixed the engine-upgrade speed-cap expression and added an empty data favicon to eliminate the browser’s favicon 404.
- `node --check game.js` passes.
- Browser tests verified shifting with clutch, driving and distance rewards, vehicle purchase, tuning/paint, day/night, pause/resume, and save persistence after reload.
- Desktop screenshot captured at `/tmp/opencode/tunis-desktop-current.png`; mobile screenshot captured at `/tmp/opencode/tunis-mobile.png`; mobile document dimensions matched the 390×844 viewport.

### Active
- Investigate mobile throttle interaction: a browser test pressing the on-screen throttle reported speed `000`, despite no overflow or page errors.
- Review mobile screenshot and perform any further interaction/layout tests as needed.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Diagnose and retest touch/pointer gameplay on mobile, including throttle, clutch, and gear shifting.
2. Review `/tmp/opencode/tunis-mobile.png` for control visibility/usability and adjust if needed.
3. Re-run `node --check game.js` and browser smoke tests after any fixes.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI structure, stylesheet, Three.js import map, and module entry point.
- `styles.css`: HUD, controls, overlays, and responsive/mobile styling.
- `game.js`: Scene, vehicles, controls, UI, progression, and render loop.
- `/tmp/opencode/tunis-desktop-current.png`: Latest desktop screenshot.
- `/tmp/opencode/tunis-mobile.png`: Latest mobile screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- Initial gear is neutral; shifting requires holding the clutch. Keyboard tests use `KeyC` for clutch and `KeyE`/`KeyQ` for shifting.
- Latest browser run had no console errors or failed network requests; purchase, tuning, paint, time-of-day, and vehicle state persisted across reload.
